put.description:
File one of the current user's saved items into one of their user collections, identified by display name.
The collection is created if it does not exist yet. A user collection is never created empty, so this call always ends with the saved item inside it.
Names are matched case-insensitively and with surrounding whitespace ignored, and the stored name is trimmed.
This operation is idempotent. If the saved item is already in the target collection nothing is written, the saved item's updated_at is left unchanged, and already_in_collection is returned true.
A name already held by a system collection, such as "Unsorted", is reserved. It returns COLLECTION_NAME_RESERVED rather than filing the saved item into a system collection.
The saved item must belong to the authenticated user. A saved item that does not exist and one owned by another user both return the same not found response, so this endpoint never discloses whether an ID exists.
Possible error codes:
- INVALID_COLLECTION_NAME
- COLLECTION_NAME_RESERVED
- BAD_REQUEST
- SAVED_ITEM_NOT_FOUND
- INVALID_AUTHORIZATION_HEADER
- INVALID_ACCESS_TOKEN
- ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRED
- INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR

parameters.name: request

400.description: Invalid collection name or saved item ID

message.example: saved item moved into collection successfully

collection_name.description:
CollectionName is the display name of the user collection to file the saved
item under. The collection is created if it does not exist yet. Names are
matched case-insensitively with surrounding whitespace ignored, and a name
already used by a system collection is rejected.

This field carries no `validate` constraint on purpose. The service owns
collection name rules and answers with the INVALID_COLLECTION_NAME code, so
a constraint here would pre-empt that and collapse both failure cases into a
generic VALIDATION_ERROR.

already_in_collection.description:
AlreadyInCollection is true when the saved item was already in the target
collection, in which case nothing was written. It is mutually exclusive with
CollectionCreated.

collection_created.description:
CollectionCreated is true only when this call created the collection. It is
false when an existing collection was reused.
